note.anchor: These ratings come only from games between the models listed here, on a scale anchored at one of them. They do not correspond to human Elo ratings, such as those of the Playdek Twilight Struggle app.
note.estimatePointer: The Playdek estimate switch shows an estimate of that scale, from games people played against these models on this site.
note.playdek: Estimates based on self-reported human ratings, not ratings from the Playdek app: each person typed in their own Playdek rating, the games were played on this site rather than in the app, and a model's rating there could differ. They come from {{games}} clean games against {{humans}} people to {{asOf}}, with takebacks allowed. Each player starts from its leaderboard gaps to the others; games against people then move it and, more loosely, the other players on its network. One whose network nobody has faced keeps its gaps alone, so its ± is wider.

codes.predates: This leaderboard.json predates the codes; rebuild it with tools/scripts/build_web.sh.
codes.note: A player's name says how it was trained: E7-A8-R1-S44 is engine E7, architecture A8, recipe R1, seed 44 (the engine it was trained on; its games here are played under the rules of the epoch shown, whatever engine trained it), and each @<step>M+<change> a branch point and what changed there (a new recipe or architecture, a seed, or a soup in parentheses). A code is a set of tools/train.py flags -- an architecture the network's shape, a recipe every other training setting -- assigned by tools/scripts/run_codes.py and listed here from research/run_codes.json (the same tables). A network is trained under the last code of each kind in its name. Recipe flags are those that differ from the defaults.
codes.showAll: Show every code, not only those of networks on the board
